description: Mary, a young Englishwoman of 18 in 1620. Sail on the Mayflower, come over later on the Anne (1623), or stay in London as a servant. Detailed context 1620-1676; the model tracks one woman's life, not the whole colony.
units: Money in units, not pounds. 20 units = one year of modest living; each place has its own cost of living. Savings are not capped.

later_ship.label: Come over later on the Anne (1623)

london.label: Stay in London as a servant

parameter_status: Every coefficient is the author's assumption. Sources support the historical context and give anchors to compare against, not these probabilities.

sources.supports: 102 passengers; sailed 16 Sept 1620; reached Cape Cod 21 Nov 1620; only 53 passengers remained after the first winter; passengers disembarked 31 March 1621
18 married women, 7 unmarried with parents, 3 young unmarried women, 1 girl, 73 men; three fourths of the women died in the first months; four women left alive by the first Thanksgiving (autumn 1621)

Fortune Nov 1621 (37 settlers); Anne and Little James July 1623 (96 settlers); population 99 Dec 1620, 50 Apr 1621; women who reached 21 lived on average to 62.4, men to 69.2; one birth in 30 killed the mother, about one woman in five died in childbirth; births about two years apart
London plague deaths: 35,000-41,313 in 1625, 10,000 in 1636, about 100,000 in 1665 (almost a quarter of London)
John Graunt, Natural and Political Observations upon the Bills of Mortality (1662): about 36% of London children died before age six; London about 384,000 people
John Demos, 'Notes on Life in Plymouth Colony', William and Mary Quarterly 22(2), 1965 - source of the Plymouth life expectancy, childbirth and family figures quoted on Wikipedia

calibration: v0.2-0.3 (04.11.2026): calibrated with episodes/mayflower-1620/analysis/calibrate.py to historical anchors, not to a storyline: three fourths of Mayflower women died the first winter; colony women who reached 21 lived on average to 62.4; about one woman in five died in childbirth; one birth in 30 killed the mother; about a quarter of London died in the 1665 plague. Fitted: first-winter death chance, birth chance per eligible year, background mortality, 1665 plague chance. v0.3 adds child survival (direct anchors, no fitting).
child_survival_note: Share of children born who grow up. Plymouth: about 7.9 of 9.3 births lived to adulthood (third generation; Wikipedia 'Plymouth Colony', after Demos). London: Graunt (1662) found about 36% of children died before age six; 0.55 to adulthood is the author's assumption built on that.
method: Full lives to death or 100. Same profile and paired seeds (world N is shared by the three paths). Exact survival/event counts; 95% Wilson intervals measure sampling, not rule accuracy. State quantiles among survivors, rounded via histograms. Examples selected by savings at 40 only.
